battery capacity = 
 INTEG( battery investment 
 - battery depreciation , init capacity batteries ) 
	~	GW
	~	Capital stock of battery. As the construction time for batteries is 1 	year, but the minimum delay time in delay fixed is TIME STEP, battery 	investment constructed is equal to battery investment.
	|

	~	GW
	~	Initial (2013) capacity of Li-ion batteries from ETRI, 2014: 1-3MW

 * gfcf shares battery[ind] 
	~	Euro constant/Year
	~	|

battery construction time = GET XLS CONSTANTS('?InputsEnvironment', 'electricity', 'battery_construction_time')
	~	Year
	~	https://lorenz-g.github.io/tesla-megapack-tracker/all-big-batteries.html: 	Sample of biggest batteries, none take longer than 12 months construction 	time.

battery cost projection lookup ( [(0,0)-(10,10)],(2010,1),(2015,1),(2020,0.55),(2025,0.34),(2030,0.23),(2040,0.16),(2045,0.15),(2050,0.14) )
	~	Dmnl
	~	Battery cost projections based on Schmidt et al., 2019, citing Schmidt et 	al., 2017.
	|

battery depreciation = 
 DELAY FIXED ( battery investment ,battery lifetime , 0) 
	~	GW/Year
	~	Storage depreciation, as a pipeline delay. As there is no inital capital, 	the initial values are set to 0.
	|

battery depreciation replacement time = 
 DELAY FIXED ( battery investment ,battery lifetime 
 - battery construction time 
 + Year 1 , 0) 
	~	GW/Year
	~	Gives the year when investment has to occur in order to counteract 	depreciation, taking into account construction time. As there is no inital 	capital, the initial values are set to 0.
	|

battery investment = 
 min ( battery investment desired , scale constraint multiplier 
 * storage max investment scale ) 
 * financial constraint factor electricity ind 
	~	GW/Year
	~	As the construction time for batteries is 1 year, but the minimum delay 	time in delay fixed is TIME STEP, battery investment constructed is equal 	to battery investment. Actual investment in storage, desired investment is 	constrained by financial resources and a maximum expansion of scale. These 	constraints can be switched off/on.
	|

battery investment costs = 
 battery investment 
 * battery investment costs per unit capacity 
	~	Euro constant/Year
	~	We assume a linear expense schedule of investment costs over the time of 	construction. But since construction time is only 1 year all is being paid 	at the moment of investment.
	|

battery investment costs per capacity initial = GET XLS CONSTANTS('?InputsEnvironment', 'electricity', 'battery_investment_costs_per_capacity_initial')
	~	Euro constant/GW
	~	Reference scenario for Li-ion batteries from ETRI, 2014. Adjusted to 2010 	Euros using core consumer price inflation from Ha et al. (2023). Due to 	very limited available capacity, we assume away learning effects between 	2010 and 2013.
	|

battery investment costs per unit capacity = 
 battery investment costs per capacity initial 
 * battery cost projection lookup ( Time 
 + initial year ) 
	~	Euro constant/GW
	~	|

battery investment costs per unit capacity learning effect = 
 battery investment costs per capacity initial 
 * battery learning effect 
	~	Euro constant/GW
	~	|

battery investment desired = 
 max ( ( required capacity batteries expected 
 - battery capacity ) 
 / inv adjustment time 
 + battery depreciation replacement time , 0) 
	~	GW/Year
	~	Desired batteries takes into account desired capital on the one hand and 	current capital stock and depreciation on the other. It adjusts the 	difference between current and desired stock over the investment 	adjustment time.
	|

battery learning effect = 
 ( max ( smooth ( battery capacity , scale impacts adjustment time ) 
 / battery capacity for learning init , 1) ) 
 ^ IF THEN ELSE ( battery capacity 
 > 0, battery learning rate beta , 0) 
	~	Dmnl
	~	The fractional impact of learning effects on investment costs. We use a 	common learning curve formulation with capacity driving improvements and a 	smooth function to reflect that learning effects don't immediately 	materialise with added capacity, but slowly evolve over time. battery 	capacity for learning init is not installed capacity in Italy but taken 	from ETRI, 2014. Thus, we assume that learning effects only take place 	when the capacity exceeds this value, but no negative effects occur if it 	is below.
	|

battery learning rate beta = GET XLS CONSTANTS('?InputsEnvironment', 'electricity', 'battery_learning_rate_beta')
	~	Dmnl
	~	Learning rate expression exponential calculted for Li-ion batteries from 	ETRI, 2014.
	|

	~	Year
	~	IEA data (IEA costs of electricity ind report 	(https://www.iea.org/reports/projected-costs-of-generating-electricity 	ind-2020)).
	|

capacity almost constructed investmen nonRES[e techn] = 
 DELAY FIXED ( capacity investment[e techn] ,capacity construction time[e techn	] 
 - Year 1 , constructed capacity investment initial[e techn] ) 
	~	GW/Year
	~	Constructed capacity for non-RES technologies are represented by a 	pipeline delay. The delay time is construction time-1 as it takes an 	additional period for capacity to accumulate in the capacity stock. The 	initial value runs until the delay time is reached, hence we assume 	constant constructed investment within this time period. As the 	construction time for RES is 1 year, but the minimum delay time in delay 	fixed is TIME STEP, RES investment constructed is equal to RES investment.
	|

 capacity investment[e solarth] 
	~	GW/Year
	~	Constructed capacity for non-RES technologies are represented by a 	pipeline delay. The delay time is construction time-1 as it takes an 	additional period for capacity to accumulate in the capacity stock. The 	initial value runs until the delay time is reached, hence we assume 	constant constructed investment within this time period. 	~	Lifetime by technology based on IEA data (IEA costs of electricity ind 	report 	(https://www.iea.org/reports/projected-costs-of-generating-electricity 	ind-2020)) and Jaxa-Rozen et al. (2022) where IEA data not available (i.e. 	for manu petroleum and bio). Due to the change of mix bewtween bio and 	geothermal in nec, the value for nec is dynamic. For simplicity we again 	assume a liner extrapolation over time. We assume solarth same as solarpv.
	|

capacity max investment scale[e techn] = 
 max scale increase[e techn] 
 * smooth ( production capacity[e techn] , scale impacts adjustment time ) 
	~	GW/Year
	~	The maximum amount that capacity can increase within a year due to limited 	production capabilities. This reflects, capital stock expansions are 	limited by current infrastructure on the ground and that the larger the 	capacity is, the larger its absolute increase can be due to more expansive 	infrastructure. The smooth function reflects that this infrastructure does 	not immediately materialise with added capacity, but slowly builds up over 	time.
	|

capacity to increase capacity under construction[e techn] :EXCEPT: [e wind], [e solarpv	], [e solarth] = 
 INTEG( actual investment to increase capacity[e techn] 
 - constructed investment to increase capacity[e techn] , ( max ( 0, constructed capacity investment initial[e techn] 
 - ( capacity initial[e techn] 
 / capacity lifetime[e techn] ) ) ) 
 * ( capacity construction time[e techn] 
 - 1) ) ~~|
capacity to increase capacity under construction[e wind] = 
 INTEG( actual investment to increase capacity[e wind] 
 - constructed investment to increase capacity[e wind] , 0) ~~|
capacity to increase capacity under construction[e solarpv] = 
 INTEG( actual investment to increase capacity[e solarpv] 
 - constructed investment to increase capacity[e solarpv] , 0) ~~|
capacity to increase capacity under construction[e solarth] = 
 INTEG( actual investment to increase capacity[e solarth] 
 - constructed investment to increase capacity[e solarth] , 0) 
	~	GW
	~	Capacity to increase capacity under construction has to be considered when 	deciding on desired investment, i.e. comparing desired capital and current 	capacity. It increases with investment and decreases with investment being 	constructed. The initial value is set as to avoid the stock from going 	below 0, since initial constructed investment to increase capacity (i.e. 	constructed capacity investment intial minus depreciatiation initial 	(which is capacity initial/capacity lifetime) flows out but never in. 	Since the initial are in a fixed delay, they run until delay time is 	reached, i.e. construction time-1 for initial constructed investment (and 	lifetime for depreciation). Thus, the initial value is only an 	initialisation simplification (the initial values will be all gone, once 	the construction time is over). As the construction time is 1 for RES, we 	do not have a delay and hence this issue with constructed investment to 	increase capacity initial, which is why we can initialize RES with 0. From 	this and the construction time-1 can be seen, this only tracks capacity 	under construction until it becomes a flow into the capacity stock. This 	stock is taken into account in the investment decision, which compares 	desired to present capacity.
	|

electricity ind demand expected = 
 IF THEN ELSE ( constrained factor delayed[electricity ind] 
 :AND: y FC delayed[electricity ind] 
 < y FE delayed[electricity ind] , unconstrained electricity ind demand expected , electricity ind demand expected constrained ) 
	~	(GW*h)/Year
	~	If capital constraint is binding, capital investment is determined by 	unconstrained expected demand as it plays role in alleviating constraint. 	If the labour constraint is binding, investment is determined by the 	constrained expected demand, since investment does not help to alleviate 	the constraint.

 * expected electricity ind demand technology share[e techn] 
	~	GW*h/Year
	~	|

electricity ind demand expected constrained = 
 electricity ind demand perceived 
 * ( 1
 + electricity ind demand expected trend 
 * ( expectations horizon 
 + expectations adjustment time ) ) 
	~	GW*h/Year
	~	The expected electricity ind demand based on trend based expectations. The 	expectations adjustment time is added to the expectation horizon in the 	exponent, as we use the perceived value as a basis. However, the perceived 	value is already delayed by the expectations adjustment time, which is why 	we add this time perdiod in the exponent. We simplify by ignoring 	compounding of the growth rate, but as the time horizon is short, this is 	a reasonable approximation.
	|

electricity ind demand expected trend = 
 ( electricity ind demand perceived 
 - electricity ind demand perceived delayed ) 
 / electricity ind demand perceived delayed 
 / expectations adjustment time 
	~	Dmnl/Year
	~	The trend formed in the expectation formation for the electricity ind 	demand.
	|

electricity ind demand perceived = 
 INTEG( electricity ind demand perceived adjustment , initial electricity ind demand ) 
	~	GW*h/Year
	~	Smoothed electricity ind demand for expectation formation.
	|

electricity ind demand perceived adjustment = 
 ( electricity ind demand 
 - electricity ind demand perceived ) 
 / expectations adjustment time 
	~	GW*h/Year/Year
	~	Adjustement of perceived electricity ind demand w.r.t. to actual observed 	electricity ind demand.
	|

electricity ind demand perceived delayed = 
 INTEG( electricity ind demand perceived delayed adjustment , initial electricity ind demand ) 
	~	GW*h/Year
	~	Smoothed electricity ind demand for expectation formation delayed, to 	calculate expectation trend.
	|

electricity ind demand perceived delayed adjustment = 
 ( electricity ind demand perceived 
 - electricity ind demand perceived delayed ) 
 / expectations adjustment time 
	~	GW*h/Year/Year
	~	Adjustement of perceived electricity ind demand delayed w.r.t. to 	electricity ind demand perceived.
	|

output expected[ind] = 
 output perceived[ind] 
 * ( 1
 + output expected trend[ind] 
 * ( expectations adjustment time ) ) 
	~	Euro constant/Year
	~	The expected electricity ind demand based on trend based expectations. The 	expectations adjustment time is added to the expectation horizon in the 	exponent, as we use the perceived value as a basis. However, the perceived 	value is already delayed by the expectations adjustment time, which is why 	we add this time perdiod in the exponent. We simplify by ignoring 	compounding of the growth rate, but as the time horizon is short, this is 	a reasonable approximation.
	|

	~	|

	~	Dmnl
	~	https://www.vensim.com/documentation/fn_allocate_by_priority.html 	"specifies how big a gap in priority is required to have the allocation go 	first to higher priority with only leftovers going to lower priority. When 	the distance between any two priorities exceeds width and the higher 	priority does not receive its full request the lower priority will receive 	nothing."

	~	The maximum amount that capacity can increase within a year due to limited 	production capabilities. This reflects, capital stock expansions are 	limited by current infrastructure on the goround and that the larger the 	capacity is, the larger its absolute increase can be due to more expansive 	infrastructure. The smooth function reflects that this infrastructure does 	not immediately materialise with added capacity, but slowly builds up over 	time. battery capacity for learning init is not installed capacity in 	Italy but taken from ETRI, 2014. Thus, we assume that scale effects 	initial refer to this value until actual capacity exceeds it.
	|

 + production by battery a ) 
 / potential production 
	~	Dmnl
	~	Since we assume that grid output increases proportional to the grid 	capital, the production share of the grid remains at its normal capacity 	utilisation. grid share electricity ind sector*uc normal D1 +(1-grid share 	electricity ind sector)*sum(production by technology b[techn!])/potential 	production Since we model the grid passibvely and it is not linked to 	production or production potential, we ignore it when calculating capacity 	utilisation. For production, utilisation is approximated as actual over 	potential production, neglecting system issues like flexibility.

	~	Euro/(Year*Person)
	~	individual disposable income by income category per capita child benefits 	were previously computed as: (ZIDZ(cb gs[female,low],L u 	gs[female,low])*People 1) +(ZIDZ(cb gs[male,low],L u gs[male,low])*People 	1) +(ZIDZ(cb gs[female,mid],L u gs[female,mid])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb 	gs[male,mid],L u gs[male,mid])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[female,hig],L u 	gs[female,hig])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[male,hig],L u gs[male,hig])*People 	1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[female,low],L gs[female,low])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb 	gs[male,low],L gs[male,low])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[female,mid],L 	gs[female,mid])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[male,mid],L gs[male,mid])*People 	1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[female,hig],L gs[female,hig])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb 	gs[male,hig],L gs[male,hig])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[female,low],N olf 	gs[female,low])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[male,low],N olf 	gs[male,low])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[female,mid],N olf 	gs[female,mid])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[male,mid],N olf 	gs[male,mid])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[female,hig],N olf 	gs[female,hig])*People 1) + (ZIDZ(cb gs[male,hig],N olf 	gs[male,hig])*People 1)
